acceptance.condition: A remote-lineage resolution error occurring after valid repository/TASK resolution but before REMEDIATION RUN creation produces a bounded local ADMISSION_FAILURE diagnostic, invokes no Executor, creates no RUN, and best-effort publishes the same diagnostic under the admission-failure remote namespace when transport is available.

Pre-RUN canonical validation failures such as invalid REVIEW/REMEDIATION lineage binding, unsupported correction admission, empty CODE_FIX scope, or empty affected verification retain the original fail-closed error while exposing the same bounded admission diagnostic with executor_invoked=false.

Repository-admission failures including dirty working tree or current HEAD not matching reviewed_sha produce the diagnostic without creating a RUN, handoff, lease, staging/result artifact, verification execution, or Executor invocation.

Published diagnostics contain only the allowlisted Runtime facts, preserve the exact bounded original error type/message, include already-known finding/review/ SHA facts when available, and never contain full stdout/stderr, secrets, source content, model prose, or semantic repair advice.

Admission diagnostic publication is immutable and idempotent for byte-identical failures; repeating the same rejected remediation does not create unbounded duplicate refs, and a different diagnostic cannot overwrite an earlier artifact.

Missing/unusable remote or a diagnostic transport failure never replaces or masks the original local admission error, never creates a RUN, and never causes retry, reroute, fallback, or an Executor call.

Once a REMEDIATION RUN has been created, subsequent execution/completion/ verification failures continue exclusively through the existing RUN-keyed FAILURE path and do not also emit a pre-RUN ADMISSION_FAILURE.
Codex and Antigravity requested remediation paths have identical pre-RUN admission-failure behavior and prove zero native executor calls for rejected admission.

A successful REMEDIATION retains the existing one-RUN/one-Executor path, affected verification, canonical ResultPackage, and post-PASS review transport without added duplicate execution or semantic reasoning.

Regression coverage proves remote-lineage, contract, dirty-repository, and reviewed-SHA admission failures; exact bounded diagnostic content; no RUN or Executor call; immutable/idempotent remote publication; unavailable/failed transport fallback; unchanged post-RUN failure transport; Executor neutrality; and unchanged successful REMEDIATION behavior.

assumptions: Current canonical AIOS-renew main baseline before TASK-047 authoring is 66a092f7341ab03519c3a463dd65caf5a6b16257.
The frozen v0.1 TASK, RUN, RESULT, EVIDENCE, REVIEW, and REMEDIATION contracts remain authoritative and unchanged.
A RUN must continue to mean an execution instance that passed admission far enough to receive canonical RUN state; pre-RUN rejection must not be represented as a RUN failure.
Existing post-RUN FAILURE persistence and transport remain the authority for failures after RUN creation.
Existing TASK-045 structured executor-diagnostic preservation and TASK-046 execution telemetry remain unchanged concerns.
Admission diagnostics are deterministic Runtime/Operator facts, not Executor claims, semantic REVIEW judgments, or a new kernel artifact family.

hard: Preserve current REMEDIATION execution semantics: all existing pre-RUN lineage, contract, executor, scope, verification, repository-cleanliness, and reviewed-SHA checks remain fail-closed, and a rejected remediation must invoke zero Executors and create zero RUNs.

When a remediation fails after the repository and TASK are validly resolved but before RUN creation, Runtime must best-effort persist one bounded local operational diagnostic under the Git runtime state and, when the configured Git remote is usable, publish the byte-exact diagnostic through an isolated remote artifact ref discoverable under refs/heads/aios/admission-failure/.

The admission diagnostic is Operator/Runtime operational state only. It must not be added to the frozen kernel schemas, must not masquerade as RESULT or EVIDENCE, and must never be consumed as semantic proof that a finding was or was not fixed.

A published diagnostic must state at minimum: kind=ADMISSION_FAILURE, operation=REMEDIATION, exact TASK id and revision, requested executor, executor_invoked=false, a bounded admission phase, and the original bounded error type/message. When already authoritatively resolved before the failure, include finding_id, review_id, reviewed_sha, and current_head_sha as exact facts rather than inferred placeholders.

Admission phase classification must remain bounded and deterministic. It may distinguish only the Runtime-owned boundaries needed to explain this flow, such as remote lineage resolution, canonical contract admission, and repository admission. It must not classify semantic root cause using a model or parse arbitrary Executor/UI prose.

Remote publication must be immutable and idempotent. Repeating the same byte-exact admission failure must not create an unbounded sequence of duplicate remote artifacts, while a materially different diagnostic must not overwrite or mutate an earlier one. Any remote-ref suffix or local identity used for this purpose must be derived deterministically from bounded diagnostic state, not clock, random, UUID, or model output.

Admission-failure persistence and publication are diagnostic side effects only. If local diagnostic persistence or remote transport itself fails, preserve the original remediation admission exception as primary, do not fabricate a RUN, do not invoke an Executor, and do not retry or replace the original error.

Do not publish secrets or unrestricted repository state. Diagnostic content must be an allowlisted bounded structure; do not include environment values, credentials, tokens, complete Git status output, complete REVIEW/REMEDIATION documents, stdout/stderr streams, or source-code contents.

Existing post-RUN FAILURE transport must remain unchanged in authority and discoverability. Once a RUN exists, failures continue through the existing RUN-keyed failure path rather than also producing an ADMISSION_FAILURE.

The implementation must be Executor-neutral. A pre-RUN rejection requested with Codex or Antigravity must have the same admission-diagnostic semantics and must record that neither Executor was invoked.

Successful REMEDIATION behavior must remain unchanged: exactly one admitted RUN, exactly one selected Executor invocation, existing completion and affected verification gates, existing ResultPackage persistence, and existing post-PASS DELTA-review transport.
README must explain the semantic distinction among admission failure, RUN failure, and post-PASS review outcome, including that an admission failure means the requested Executor never ran.
Do not push from executor execution.

task.goal: Close the observed AIOS-renew REMEDIATION pre-dispatch observability gap by preserving and publishing a bounded Runtime-owned admission-failure diagnostic when a valid Human-authorized remediation command fails before RUN admission and before any Executor invocation. The diagnostic must let ChatGPT distinguish "remediation was rejected before execution" from an Executor or completion failure without creating a fake RUN, weakening fail-closed validation, adding retries, or changing the frozen kernel contracts.
non_goals: Change or unfreeze TASK, RUN, RESULT, EVIDENCE, REVIEW, REMEDIATION, or REPAIR schemas or semantics.
Create a RUN, RESULT, staging ResultPackage, handoff, lease, or Executor invocation for a remediation rejected before admission.
Generalize this task to PRIMARY, REPAIR, Direct Candidate Acceptance, task authoring, queues, watchers, or every possible Operator command.
Change remote canonical remediation lineage semantics, finding semantics, reviewed-SHA authority, repository gates, affected verification, or post-PASS DELTA review.
Add retry, reroute, fallback, automatic remediation, automatic repair, another Executor, planner, supervisor, background worker, database, metrics service, or analytics pipeline.
Transport full stdout, stderr, stack traces, model transcripts, chat history, arbitrary UI text, or free-form Executor prose as admission diagnostics.
Let Runtime decide whether the semantic finding is fixed, suggest implementation changes, or reinterpret REVIEW/REMEDIATION content.
Make remote diagnostic publication a prerequisite that can replace or mask the original admission failure when Git transport is unavailable.
Add clock-, random-, UUID-, or process-global identity solely to name admission-failure artifacts.
task.problem: Normal REMEDIATION now persists and transports failures once a RUN has been created, but several authoritative checks still occur before RUN creation: remote REVIEW/REMEDIATION lineage resolution, contract validation, executor and correction-scope admission, affected-verification admission, repository cleanliness, and reviewed-SHA binding. If one of these checks fails, the local Operator/Antigravity UI reports the error but no canonical remote diagnostic is available to ChatGPT because the existing failure path is keyed to a created RUN. This leaves execution semantics correct and fail-closed while creating a control- plane blind spot that can cause the Human or Reviewer to misread the state and repeat a fix that was never admitted. TASK-047 must close only that observed REMEDIATION admission gap in the Operator/Runtime layer.
